luaThirdpartyInventory.licenseConclusion: All three pinned top-level Lua version trees contain lua.h whose end-of-file notice states the Lua.org, PUC-Rio copyright and standard MIT permission/warranty text. The repository-root listing had no LICENSE; the per-file headers provide the relevant notice evidence for these representative core headers. This does not establish that every file has identical notices or that no separately copyrighted components exist.

coverageAndLimitations: This document supplements, and does not replace, the ten direct Trime gitlinks in vendor/native-source-pins.json.

The six librime dependency gitlinks are pinned by librime commit 56737cd29a4d393a104a2098ece3697aa2810465 and exact tree entries, but no source trees were downloaded and their nested dependencies/licenses were not recursively audited.
The three Lua trees are identified and their representative lua.h file headers are verified; per-file notice coverage across every C/header file remains unverified.
CMake requirements and deps.mk are upstream source metadata; they do not prove which dependency versions/options were used to produce Trime's distributed Android native binaries.

The ten direct Trime pins plus six librime nested pins are not the complete native corresponding-source/dependency graph. In particular Boost and toolchain inputs are not exactly pinned here; other plugin-specific build inputs may remain. This inventory does not prove that the precompiled JNI libraries are reproducible or byte-identical.

No source trees were cloned or downloaded; only small text metadata/headers were fetched. No build, install, ADB, fork, or license acceptance was performed. This inventory is provenance evidence, not legal advice or a conclusion that redistribution requirements are satisfied.
